reviews.text: Finally: an affordable game made for regular people. Fight the oligarchmages and save democracy.
Spent ~30 hours playing the demo and can confidently recommend. One of the most promising and engaging autobattlers I've played- on the same level of addictiveness as Hearthstone BGs and The Bazaar.
Every game is a unique optimization puzzle which really tickles my brain just right.

Fun, Relaxing Game with a lot of depth. First game in history to not have sound and music on 100% when I launched. Possibly the best game dev decision ever made, give these guys millions for revolutionary ideas such as this.
sometimes i play this game so long i forget to use the bathroom, call it Project SkyShart
Very fun game that is getting regular updates. A lot of depth which leads to a steep learning curve. Great art makes even weak runs fun.
Great game. Took me a little bit of work to start learning how to play the game. Still not great at the game, but its a mellow game and holds my attention. Nice work Ben and Regis!

I dont normally play games like this often but after putting 8 hours into the demo i figured maybe this would be a game for me and it is gameplay wise but after hour 10 or so i started getting put up against cities that felt like they had choices wildly superior to mine. The last 3 hours out of my 13 hours of playtime have been over 90 percent losses and and just horrendous luck on a lot of choices in game. When i played the demo i didnt have access to every building available so most builds i could make were much easier to get just because of my available choices. In the full game you get a wider variety of choices which means a greater chance of getting screwed over by RNG however before the latest patch i kept seeing the same two to three builds over and over and over and if you dont get a handful of combos possible youre just gonna lose before or around turn ten. Ive been getting more and more frustrated at the game and even after taking a break from it for a few days and coming back after the latest patch ive been having almost the exact same experience. With all that said i still cant put it at a not recommend. The problems im having could be mostly because of skill issue so im going to dive deeper into the game and see if something clicks that im missing. Im glad we have the option of getting play stellar games by indie devs and i dont want to push anyone away from this game with a negative review when i do think it can be a great game and problems i have with it could be just personal preference but i have to air out problems ive been having with this game that might push some people away. Also the game was 15 bucks and i spent 13 hours in it not including my playtime with the demo which initially got me to buy the game. I would say i got my moneys worth even if the last 3 hours i was having a miserable time playing. I plan on playing a bit more to see if maybe my rng changes or i just somehow understand the game more or something that would make experiences in the last three hours less of an issue.

I watched ItsBen321 play Backpack Battles for so long, and had high hopes when I heard about this game. I also watched RegisKillbin play Hearthstone for years. I do think this game is a testament to the small guy achieving their dreams, and that counts for something. But as far as the substance of Skyshard, standing on its own two feet, the game kinda blows. The art style has no great consistency, and the game seems to be littered with WIP stand-in art that looks like a 3rd grader drew it on a time limit. The game isn't very well balanced, many units feel completely useless in 99% of scenarios, and most late game builds revolve around the same handful of absolutely broken generically good units (Forcefield being chief among those) After a few games I didn't feel like I was seeing anything really new, and the formula breaking choices this game made of having a much larger playing field with many more units did not add anything to my enjoyment of the genre. It just feels much harder to wrap my head around synergies and intended (or unintended) combos. There is also a VERY large element of luck in this game, in that you roll for a subset of options (Ex: A tier 2-3 nature unit) and then roll within that subset. I don't feel like I have much control over the outcomes or directions of the build, at least not more than just taking the best options I get offered, which is the video game equivalent of going the way the wind blows me. That isn't strategy, it is a barely interesting casino but without the satisfying payoff. I can't in good faith recommend this game, which disappoints me greatly.

Love it, some QOL on building placement is necessary as there are many to manage (like why not include "square selection" to move multiple buildings at once ? ) this is a serious competitor to games like The Bazaar (which i play a lot a lot), but sadly low budget :D. gratz for this early access, and i'm not even a Regis fan.

When I heard from Regis himself that he and Ben were releasing a game, I was very eager to try it out. I've watched a good bit of Bazaar content, and so I was primed for an enjoyable experience with notably less polish. What I was not expecting, however, was to find a game that, despite its budgetary constraints, genuinely felt like it gave Bazaar a run for its money. I absolutely adore games like Iron Lung, Signalis, and Lunacid, the kind of small-team indie games that feel great to play, and have so much heart. They have rapidly become some of my most memorable gaming experiences, and I'm glad to find another to add to that list.
I purchased this game before the 4th of July holiday. All I could think about while celebrating with friends and family was getting back home so I could play this game. Super fun.

I feel bad writing this because I watch Regis's content and wanted to support but... there is just very little satisfaction in building these islands. As an experiment, I tried just grabbing random units and never reading what they did and I had about equal success as when I tried to build a cohesive team

Mechanics are a bit overwhelming but I enjoy the visual cues that help players get better at the game. It's kinda like playing tetris but the pieces are trying to shoot each other at the same time. Can't wait for the full release with full art for all the units and maybe some new heroes too.

Big fan of Regis through YT and wanted to check this game out after watching a few of his run-throughs. There is definitely a learning curve to this game. My frazzled ADD brain is able to pick up on some things quick, but other things take longer to figure out. But there is DEPTH in this game. I've mostly focused on Town, Nature, and Magic units (I've only played two days, guys), but want to branch out to the others already. I am hoping that I don't learn everything there is to know about the game in a week. Also, unlike a certain other game I quit playing, the game length for the runs is long enough that I feel content doing one and then moving on with my day yet engaging enough that I'm making the most of my time playing. Looking forward to the developments of the in-game art and future additions, especially if there are more characters planned down the line! UPDATE: Still recommend the game, but there are some definite imbalanced combos in the game that you have to get LUCKY to come across. There's no clear "winning strategy" when you are randomly given an assortment of stores to pick from, so while it can be strategic, there is a defined luck element to the game... which sours it for me when I try to put together what I think will win only to get wiped off the map without it even being close. I wish I had a suggestion, since there IS a tutorial you can use AND a library to compare units you've seen. But most of that becomes moot if you don't come across the units you need for your strategy.
If you like Oaken Tower, need to grab this! Cannot wait for more content, currently addicted.
Great Game! Lot's of strategies to explore and I still feel like I find new things to try almost every run. Would love to have a way to replay runs or at least battles :)
Not the simplest game but in a very rewarding way, Ill keep playing :)
A very solid auto battler, haven't been able to put it down since playing the demo, very much reminds me of the bazaar and Hearthstone battlegrounds.
It's a fun pvp autobattler. Lot of complexity.
Very solid game, easy to learn with a lot of skill expression

Really fun game with a lot of depth. There's some interactions/synergies that I only figured out after many hours and probably more that haven't even been discovered yet. Definitley takes a while to figure out what builds work well but it's also just fun to mess around. The game is getting frequent updates and has an active Discord server where the devs take feedback and communicate with the players. The people in the discord are also just really nice and like to help / answer questions :)

While I did refund this game, I recommend it for anyone new to the Inventory Management Auto Battler world. It's a great introduction to the genre, and they did a lot of things right. I don't think this necessarily revolutionized the genre though. For anyone that's played the backpack series of games or monsters & dungeons or what have you---there isn't much to gain from this, at least in its current state.
